Borane/Transition Metal−Catalyzed Allenylic and Allylic Alkylation
of Unactivated 2‑Alkylbenzoxazoles

ABSTRACT: Asymmetric functionalization of unactivated alkyl-
substituted azaarenes at the α-position of the alkyl substituent is
challenging because deprotonation of the weakly acidic α-C−H
bonds requires a strong base. This requirement often impedes
effective enantiocontrol by chiral catalysts. As a result, the few
reactions that have been reported have narrow substrate scopes.
Herein, we report a method for highly diastereo- and
enantioselective allenylic alkylation reactions of unactivated 2-
alkylbenzoxazoles with conjugated enynes, enabled by synergistic
borane/nickel catalysis. The success of this method hinges on
catalytic activation of the 2-alkylbenzoxazoles by a triarylborane,
which permits deprotonation by triethylamine and thus is crucial for achieving both high yields and diastereo- and
enantioselectivities. Extending the utility of synergistic borane/transition metal catalysis, we also demonstrate that a borane/
palladium system effectively overcomes the limitations of palladium-catalyzed allylic alkylation reactions of unactivated azaarenes. In
particular, previously unreactive acyclic 1,3-disubstituted allylic esters are rendered viable electrophiles, enabling the construction of
products bearing two adjacent stereocenters.
■
INTRODUCTION
Azaarene moieties substituted with alkyl groups containing
carbon stereogenic centers are common in pharmaceuticals,
agrochemicals, and natural products.
1
Direct functionalization
of azaarenes at the α-position of a linear alkyl substituent via
deprotonation with a base and electrophilic trapping of the
resulting carbanion is the most straightforward strategy for
constructing such structures. Although non-enantioselective
variants of these reactions that afford racemic products are well
developed,
2
catalytic enantioselective counterparts have largely
been limited to azaarenes activated by electron-withdrawing
groups
3−5
(Scheme 1a), which can be readily deprotonated
with a relatively weak base (e.g., DBU or NEt
3
). In contrast,
deprotonation of unactivated azaarenes requires a strong base
(e.g.,
n
BuLi or lithium bis(trimethylsilyl)amide), use of which
increases not only the likelihood of uncatalyzed background
reactions but also the possibility of chiral catalyst decom-
position. Notably, the few successful examples of catalytic
asymmetric reactions involving unactivated azaarenes have
primarily been metal-catalyzed allylic alkylation reactions,
typically employing metal-π-allyl electrophiles generated in
situ.
6
Other classes of electrophiles are rarely reported.
7
To
overcome these limitations and expand the range of compatible
electrophiles, alternative strategies are required.
Hydrometalation of conjugated enynes has been reported to
generate exo-alkylidene-metal-π-allyl electrophiles that can be
coupled enantioselectively with various nucleophiles to afford
structurally diverse allenes in the presence of a chiral metal
catalyst (Scheme 1b).
3c,8
However, reported examples of such
coupling reactions are limited to relatively acidic pronucleo-
philes, which can be readily deprotonated by a relatively weak
base to generate the corresponding nucleophile. The resulting
protonated base may then shuttle the proton either to the
metal catalyst, forming a metal hydride that subsequently
hydrometallates the enyne,
3c,8a,b,d,e
or directly to the metalated
enyne;
8c
both pathways ultimately afford the electrophile. In
contrast, deprotonation of less acidic pronucleophiles requires
stronger bases and generates proton-locked conjugate acids
that are ineffective at transferring the proton. This inhibition of
electrophile formation renders unactivated alkyl-substituted
azaarenes unsuitable as pronucleophiles in metal-catalyzed
reactions with conjugated enynes.
Based on these analyses, we hypothesized that strategies to
enhance the α-C−H acidity of unactivated alkylazaarenes
would enable their deprotonation by a relatively weak base,

thereby allowing coupling with conjugated enynes under metal
catalysis. Furthermore, employing a chiral metal catalyst could
render the transformation enantioselective, thereby broadening
the range of compatible electrophiles for the enantioselective
α-functionalization of unactivated azaarenes. Notably, the
Wasa group and our group recently developed various
synthetic methods based on increasing the acidity of
pronucleophiles by means of borane activation.
7f,9
In
particular, in a prior study, our group demonstrated that a
borane catalyst not only can activate azaarenes but also
remains catalytically competent despite strong coordination by
the nitrogen atom of the azaarene.
7f
This finding can be
attributed to steric hindrance around the borane center, which
promotes frustrated Lewis pair−type behavior.
10
We thus
envisioned that borane activation of azaarenes could be utilized
to accomplish unprecedented allenylic alkylation reactions of
unactivated azaarenes with enynes. Indeed, we herein report
that the desired transformation can be achieved by using a
previously unreported synergistic borane/nickel catalytic
system (Scheme 1c). The reactions exhibit a broad substrate
scope and high diastereo- and enantioselectivities. In addition,
we found that borane activation can be used for overcoming
the limitations of palladium-catalyzed asymmetric allylic
alkylation reactions of azaarenes.
■
RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
We commenced our study with the allenylic alkylation reaction
of benzoxazole 1a (1.0 equiv) with enyne 2a (1.5 equiv)
(Table 1). Initial screening focused on reactions involving
chiral phosphine ligands L1−L4 in the presence of triethyl-
amine as the base and B(C

SL-J009-1 (L4) were catalytically active. Among them, L4
provided the best outcome, affording product 3a in 36% NMR
yield with a 7:1 diastereomer ratio (dr) and 97% enantiomeric
excess (ee) (entry 4). Subsequent screening of boron-based
Lewis acids LA1−LA4 (entries 5−7), which differ in Lewis
acidity and steric bulk, in reactions with L4 as the ligand
revealed that the Lewis acid’s properties markedly affected the
yield and diastereoselectivity. The use of LA1, which is
sterically demanding and highly acidic (acceptor number (AN)
= 83.4),
11
improved the yield from 36% (with LA3) to 69%
and the dr from 7:1 to 12:1 (entry 5). LA2, which is less
sterically demanding than LA3 because of the absence of ortho
fluorine atoms, gave a lower yield and poorer diastereose-
lectivity (entry 6). LA4, which is less acidic (AN = 70.6)
9c
than
LA3, was inactive (entry 7). The stronger Lewis acidity of LA1
may have resulted in better activation of 1a, and this acid’s
steric bulk facilitated frustrated Lewis pair-type interactions
with both 1a and trimethylamine, interactions that were
important for catalytic turnover. Lowering the reaction
temperature from 22 to 10 °C and extending the reaction
time from 24 to 36 h markedly enhanced both the yield and
the diastereoselectivity and maintained the high ee (entry 8).
Reducing the nickel catalyst loading from 10 to 5 mol %
maintained the selectivity but modestly reduced the yield
(entry 9). Notably, with 5 mol % of the nickel catalyst, scaling
up the reaction from 0.1 to 0.2 mmol of 1a and increasing the
loading of 2a to 2.0 equiv afforded 3a in 85% isolated yield
with >20:1 dr and 99% ee (entry 10). Control experiments
confirmed that neither the borane catalyst nor the nickel

Replacement of the 2-ethyl group in 1a with
n
propyl,
n
pentyl,
or phenethyl groups afforded products 3b−3d in good yields
with excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivities. When R
2
was
i
propyl, the increased steric bulk led to diminished reactivity
and diastereoselectivity, affording product 3e in 20% yield and
1.5:1 dr, while maintaining high ee values for both
diastereomers. The use of 2-methylbenzoxazole also resulted
in a low yield of the desired product (3f, 29%) along with a
dialkylation byproduct in 10% yield (not shown in Table 2). In
contrast, when the
i
propyl or cyclopentyl group was positioned
one carbon further along the alkyl chain, the reactions
proceeded smoothly to give 3g and 3h in high yields.
Furthermore, 2-alkyl chains bearing terminal ester, trifluor-
omethyl, phenoxy, acetoxy, or benzoyloxy substituent were
well tolerated, affording products 3i−3m in 54−94% yields
with excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivities (up to >20:1
dr and 99% ee). The diastereo- and enantioselectivity
remained high across a range of benzoxazoles bearing diverse
aryl ring substituents at various positions (3n−3v). Notably,
benzoxazoles bearing ester substituents (1q and 1t) failed to
furnish the corresponding products (3q and 3t) under
conditions without LA1, indicating that the ester group
could not provide the same activation as the borane catalyst.
Aryl-substituted enynes bearing various electron-donating or
electron-withdrawing groups at the ortho, meta, or para
position of the benzene ring were compatible with the reaction
conditions; products 4b−4h were obtained in 65−89% yields
with high diastereo- and enantioselectivities. 2-Naphthyl-, 3-
thienyl-, and alkyl-substituted enynes also underwent the
reaction, affording target products 4i−4l with high diastereo-
and enantioselectivities. The absolute configuration of 4m was
determined by X-ray crystallography of a single crystal. The
scope of this reaction is presently confined to benzoxazoles
(see the Supporting Information for incompatible heteroar-
enes).
The allenylic alkylation reaction was readily scaled up: the
reaction of 1a (5.0 mmol) with 2l (10.0 mmol) afforded 4l in
84% yield with 11:1 dr and 99% ee (Scheme 2). Desilylation of
4l with tetrabutylammonium fluoride provided 5 in 82% yield.
Subsequent gold-catalyzed intramolecular cyclization
3c,12
of 5
via hydroxyl attack on the allene furnished 6 in 78% yield as
the E-olefin exclusively, with retention of both dr and ee. In
contrast, N-iodosuccinimide-mediated cyclization
13
of 5 gave 7
in 90% yield with the Z-olefin as the major isomer (Z/E =
6.3:1), also with retention of dr and ee.
On the basis of literature precedents,
8c,9
we propose that
these reactions proceed by a mechanism involving the
interconnected catalytic cycles shown in Scheme 3. In the
boron cycle, the borane catalyst enhances the acidity of the α-
C−H bonds of the 2-alkylbenzoxazole by coordinating to the
nitrogen atom. Subsequent deprotonation by triethylamine
gives a borane-ligated carbanion (or aza-enolate),
14
which acts
as a nucleophile in the coupling reaction. In the nickel cycle,
the alkyne moiety undergoes oxidative addition to Ni(0) to
generate a three-membered Ni(II)−olefin ring,
8c
which is
subsequently protonated by the conjugate acid of the base to
furnish a vinylnickel species. This species undergoes a rapid
σ−π rearrangement to generate the key exo-alkylidene-Ni(II)-
π-allyl electrophile. Outer-sphere attack by the nucleophile on
the electrophile gives the product,
15
simultaneously regenerat-
ing the borane and nickel catalysts.
Inspired by the success of synergistic borane/nickel catalysis
of allenylic alkylation reactions of unactivated 2-alkylbenzox-
azoles, we explored the applicability of catalytic systems
involving borane and other transition metals to asymmetric
allylic alkylation reactions of unactivated azaarenes, which
remain challenging, particularly for the construction of
products with two adjacent stereogenic centers. To date,
only two examples of the formation of compounds with vicinal
stereocenters have been reported,
6a,b
both of which are
restricted to cyclic allylic esters�likely because the steric
hindrance associated with acyclic systems decreases their
reactivity. We hypothesized we could overcome this challenge
of poor reactivity of acyclic allylic esters by tuning the borane
catalyst.
Through optimization of the reaction conditions (see
Supporting Information), we found that a borane/palladium
system efficiently catalyzed asymmetric allylation of 2-
alkylbenzoxazoles with racemic 1,3-disubstituted acyclic allylic
pivalates to form products with vicinal stereocenters (Table 3).

Notably, the use of TESBr was crucial to the success of these
allylic alkylation reactions; in the absence of this additive, the
yield of 9a was only 5% in otherwise identical conditions.
Furthermore, using 1.0 equiv of LA4 without TESBr resulted
in a 60% yield of 9a (see Supporting Information). Gas
chromatography−mass spectrometry revealed that the stand-
ard reaction conditions afforded a considerable amount of
TESOPiv. Because the pivalate anion coordinates more
strongly than bromide to the borane catalyst, owing to the
better interaction of the oxygen 2p lone pair with the empty
boron 2p orbital, TESBr may enhance catalyst turnover by
scavenging the pivalate anion after product formation.
■
CONCLUSIONS
In conclusion, we used synergistic borane/transition metal
catalysis to overcome the challenges posed by asymmetric
functionalization of unactivated alkylazaarenes at the α-
position of the alkyl substituent. This strategy allowed us to
achieve the first examples of coupling reactions between
unactivated 2-alkylbenzoxazoles and conjugated enynes, which
were promoted by a borane/nickel catalytic system and
afforded previously elusive compounds with 1,3-nonadjacent
stereocenters. Moreover, diastereo- and enantioselective
asymmetric allylic alkylation reactions of unactivated 2-
alkylbenzoxazoles with acyclic 1,3-disubstituted allylic esters
were achieved with a borane/palladium system. A key element
of both transformations is the use of fluorinated triarylboranes,
which enable base-mediated deprotonation of otherwise poorly
acidic α-C−H bonds under mild conditions. The method has a
broad substrate scope, allowing reactions of diverse 2-
alkylbenzoxazoles and electrophiles (>60 examples). Our
work not only provides powerful solutions for accessing
complex chiral architectures bearing multiple stereocenters
from readily available precursors but also establishes synergistic
borane/transition metal catalysis as a versatile strategy for
asymmetric functionalization reactions.

ABSTRACT: Asymmetric functionalization of unactivated alkyl-
substituted azaarenes at the α-position of the alkyl substituent is
challenging because deprotonation of the weakly acidic α-C−H
bonds requires a strong base. This requirement often impedes
efective enantiocontrol by chiral catalysts. As a result, the few
reactions that have been reported have narrow substrate scopes.
Herein, we report a method for highly diastereo- and
enantioselective allenylic alkylation reactions of unactivated 2-
alkylbenzoxazoles with conjugated enynes, enabled by synergistic
borane/nickel catalysis. The success of this method hinges on
catalytic activation of the 2-alkylbenzoxazoles by a triarylborane,

■ INTRODUCTION

Azaarene moieties substituted with alkyl groups containing
carbon stereogenic centers are common in pharmaceuticals,
agrochemicals, and natural products.<sup>1</sup> Direct functionalization
of azaarenes at the α-position of a linear alkyl substituent via
deprotonation with a base and electrophilic trapping of the
resulting carbanion is the most straightforward strategy for
constructing such structures. Although non-enantioselective
variants of these reactions that aford racemic products are well
developed,<sup>2</sup> catalytic enantioselective counterparts have largely
been limited to azaarenes activated by electron-withdrawing
groups<sup>3−5</sup> (Scheme 1a), which can be readily deprotonated
with a relatively weak base (e.g., DBU or NEt ). In contrast,
deprotonation of unactivated azaarenes requires a strong base
(e.g., <sup>n</sup>BuLi or lithium bis(trimethylsilyl)amide), use of which
increases not only the likelihood of uncatalyzed background
reactions but also the possibility of chiral catalyst decom-
position. Notably, the few successful examples of catalytic
asymmetric reactions involving unactivated azaarenes have
primarily been metal-catalyzed allylic alkylation reactions,
typically employing metal-π-allyl electrophiles generated in
situ.<sup>6</sup> Other classes of electrophiles are rarely reported.<sup>7</sup> To
overcome these limitations and expand the range of compatible
electrophiles, alternative strategies are required.

Hydrometalation of conjugated enynes has been reported to
generate exo-alkylidene-metal-π-allyl electrophiles that can be

coupled enantioselectively with various nucleophiles to aford
structurally diverse allenes in the presence of a chiral metal
catalyst (Scheme 1b).<sup>3c,8</sup> However, reported examples of such
coupling reactions are limited to relatively acidic pronucleo-
philes, which can be readily deprotonated by a relatively weak
base to generate the corresponding nucleophile. The resulting
protonated base may then shuttle the proton either to the
metal catalyst, forming a metal hydride that subsequently
hydrometallates the enyne,<sup>3c,8a,b,d,e</sup> or directly to the metalated
enyne;<sup>8c</sup> both pathways ultimately aford the electrophile. In
contrast, deprotonation of less acidic pronucleophiles requires
stronger bases and generates proton-locked conjugate acids
that are inefective at transferring the proton. This inhibition of
electrophile formation renders unactivated alkyl-substituted
azaarenes unsuitable as pronucleophiles in metal-catalyzed
reactions with conjugated enynes.

enhance the α-C−H acidity of unactivated alkylazaarenes
would enable their deprotonation by a relatively weak base,

Inspired by the success of synergistic borane/nickel catalysis

involving borane and other transition metals to asymmetric
allylic alkylation reactions of unactivated azaarenes, which

restricted to cyclic allylic esters�likely because the steric

reactivity. We hypothesized we could overcome this challenge

catalyst.

■ CONCLUSIONS

In conclusion, we used synergistic borane/transition metal
catalysis to overcome the challenges posed by asymmetric
functionalization of unactivated alkylazaarenes at the α-
position of the alkyl substituent. This strategy allowed us to
achieve the first examples of coupling reactions between
unactivated 2-alkylbenzoxazoles and conjugated enynes, which
were promoted by a borane/nickel catalytic system and
aforded previously elusive compounds with 1,3-nonadjacent
stereocenters. Moreover, diastereo- and enantioselective
asymmetric allylic alkylation reactions of unactivated 2-
alkylbenzoxazoles with acyclic 1,3-disubstituted allylic esters
were achieved with a borane/palladium system. A key element
of both transformations is the use of fluorinated triarylboranes,
which enable base-mediated deprotonation of otherwise poorly
acidic α-C−H bonds under mild conditions. The method has a
broad substrate scope, allowing reactions of diverse 2-
alkylbenzoxazoles and electrophiles (>60 examples). Our
work not only provides powerful solutions for accessing
complex chiral architectures bearing multiple stereocenters
from readily available precursors but also establishes synergistic
borane/transition metal catalysis as a versatile strategy for
asymmetric functionalization reactions.
